subject: MAP: performance testing plan and concurrency findings for Sigma Health
summary: Mutual action plan (MAP) coordination for performance benchmarking with Sigma Health. Agreed test matrix (latency, throughput, TTFT), concurrency plan (burst vs steady-state), and recommended rate-limit tuning. Final results attached: steady-state target met at 250 concurrent streams, observed p95 latency 430ms under sustained load; burst tests revealed queue growth beyond 600 req/s and TTFT regressions. Recommended production rate limits and queue caps included.

High level response and plan attached: redwood_concurrency_test_plan.pdf (see attachment). Key bullets here:

Hi all — prepping the test matrix and wanted to share specifics so you can validate before we run in sandbox: 

Planned test matrix (short):
- Steady-state: 8h window simulated via traffic generator with ramp to 250 concurrent streams (interleaved requests per user). Run duration: 2h for baseline, 8h overnight for 8-hour pattern.
- Burst (short): 60s spike to 650 req/s, repeated 3x with 5m cool-downs.
- Burst (long): 10m sustained at 350 req/s.
- Payloads: sample prompt set A (50p), prompt set B (structured tool calls, 30p).
- Models: open-v1 (baseline), open-v1-quant (lower-cost), redwood-fallback (smaller architecture) for graceful degradation behavior.

Observability we will capture: request timestamps, server queue depth, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, tokens/sec, TTFT per request, p50/p95/p99 for generation latency. We'll publish a CSV with aggregated stats (concurrency_results_q1.csv).

Quick note on thresholds we suggest for MAP:
- Steady-state pass: p95 generation latency <= 430ms (tighter than initial ask — this is our target for the model/config we recommend), TTFT median <= 200ms.
- Burst behavior: system should avoid unbounded queue growth; queue cap at 1000 requests with backpressure/retry-after header preferred. If queue > 1000, fallback to smaller model and return degraded shape with clear signal.

Can Sigma confirm the two prompt sets and whether tool-calling flows in B are acceptable for non-prod runs?

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Team — quick summary after sandbox runs (attachments: concurrency_results_q1.csv, ttft_latency_summary.txt):

What we ran: 1/18 steady-state 2h baseline at 250 concurrent streams; 1/19 burst window tests: short 60s spikes to 650 req/s (3x) and long 10m spike at 350 req/s. Workloads included the large-token batched prompts Marcus called out.

Key findings (short bullets):
- Steady-state: sustained 250 concurrent streams achieved. Observed throughput ~46k tokens/sec aggregated. Median TTFT = 185ms; p95 TTFT = 360ms. Generation p95 latency = 412ms, p99 = 780ms (these correspond to heavy tail under pathological prompts).
- Burst short (60s -> 650 req/s): queue began to increase noticeably after 22s into the spike; peak queue length reached ~1,100 requests before we triggered fallback. During the period when queue >1000, TTFT median rose to 620ms and p95 generation latency to ~1.2s. We validated model fallback logic — traffic routed to redwood-fallback variant reduced p95 to ~540ms and lowered queue growth.
- Burst long (10m -> 350 req/s): system held steady for ~6m then queue growth slowly increased; GPU utilization averaged 92%. Degraded responses increased (~4% requests returned fallback variant).

Recommendations for MAP and production config:
1) Production rate-limiting: token-based soft limit combined with per-tenant RPS cap. Suggested baseline: soft token rate 1,200,000 tokens/min per tenant with RPS cap 450 req/s and burst allowance up to 700 req/s with short-term queue cap of 1,000. Return Retry-After when queue cap hit and concurrently initiate model-fallback.
2) Queue handling: enforce hard queue cap 1,200; use circuit-breaker to start fail-fast to preserve SLOs when sustained queue growth for >30s.
3) TTFT/latency targets for MAP: set steady-state p95 generation latency target = 450ms, TTFT median <= 220ms. These are realistic given our current recommended config and model variants.
4) MAP timeline: incorporate test results into Sigma_MAP_v3.xlsx, update procurement docs; target final MAP sign-off 2026-02-03 to meet your Feb 5 procurement close.

Next steps / action owners:
- Redwood (Aisha): upload consolidated CSV and summary (done).
- Sigma (Selena & Marcus): confirm you accept recommended rate limits for production MAP (reply by 1/23).
- Redwood (Priyom): create a short runbook snippet for orgs on how to configure token-based limits + model-fallback in Private deployments.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if you want to walk through graphs.

Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
